name: MAD
description: Adversarial training (AT) is a prominent technique employed by deep learning models to defend against adversarial attacks, and to some extent, enhance model robustness. However, there are three main drawbacks of the existing AT-based defense methods: expensive computational cost, low generalization ability, and the dilemma between the original model and the defense model. To this end, we propose a novel benchmark called meta adversarial defense (MAD). The MAD benchmark consists of two MAD datasets, along with a MAD evaluation protocol. The two large-scale MAD datasets were generated through experiments using 30 kinds of attacks on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets. In addition, we introduce a meta-learning based adversarial training (Meta-AT) algorithm as the baseline, which features high robustness to unseen adversarial attacks through few-shot learning. reputation: A niche but relevant benchmark in adversarial robustness research, mainly used to evaluate meta-learning-based defenses rather than as a broad community standard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on adversarial defense; results depend heavily on attack set, threat model, and whether attacks are seen or unseen.
